title: I Forwarded the Group-Chat Roast to the Boss They Thought Wasn't Added

parts.text: I was added to a side chat called leadership-adj at 12:19. It was not leadership. It was three teammates roasting our boss's stutter and planning to tank her project so "someone competent" could take it. I was twenty-six. I had a stutter as a kid. I screenshotted, left, and sat with a sandwich that turned to cardboard. Then they posted a meme in the main channel with the same joke, tagged with a gif of her presenting.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The private roast just went public as a gif on her presentation.

social.video_title: They planned to tank her project in a chat they thought was sealed — Part 1/2
social.description: Wrongly added, cardboard sandwich, stutter jokes. Then a gif. Would you have stayed silent?

parts.text: I forwarded the screenshots to her and to HR the same minute. I will not pretend I agonized for days. She deserved the packet. HR ran it. Two people left the company. One stayed and stopped being funny. Her project shipped. I eat sandwiches that taste like food again. Side chats are still allowed. Cruelty as strategy is not a competency I need to protect.

social.video_title: The packet went to her before the gif could harden — Part 2/2
social.description: Project shipped, jokes unemployed, sandwich restored. Was a stutter a performance plan?
